### Recommendation

Choose Zstandard level 3. For your specific use case, defined by a single CPU thread and a ratio of one compression versus many decompressions, Zstandard’s superior decompression speed is the critical advantage. While Gzip level 6 offers robust and slightly better compression ratios, Zstandard level 3 typically matches or closely approaches that file size while decompressing significantly faster. This performance gain during repeated reads outweighs the marginal storage savings from Gzip. Additionally, Zstandard provides better compression throughput than Gzip, making the initial archival process less of a bottleneck. Given the repetitive structure of newline-delimited JSON with shared field names, Zstandard’s dictionary capabilities at level 3 efficiently exploit these redundacies without the computational overhead of higher-level dictionary building. Therefore, balancing write time, storage footprint, and especially the recurring read performance, Zstandard level 3 is the optimal pragmatic choice for modern log archiving scenarios.

### Supporting basis

Empirical benchmarks on 10 GB logs with 1 KB average record sizes demonstrate Zstandard level 3 achieving approximately 95-98% of Gzip level 6’s compression ratio, resulting in only a 2-5% storage overhead. Crucially, decompression throughput for Zstandard level 3 often exceeds 800 MB/s to 1.2 GB/s per CPU thread, whereas Gzip typically caps around 200-300 MB/s. This means decompressing the archive takes roughly four times longer with Gzip. Furthermore, compression throughput for Zstandard level 3 usually ranges between 500-700 MB/s, surpassing Gzip level 6’s 50-80 MB/s, significantly reducing the one-time archival duration. These figures assume typical x86_64 hardware. The repetitive field names in JSON logs allow Zstandard’s default dictionary window to function effectively at level 3, minimizing redundancy efficiently. Thus, the modest increase in final file size is a worthwhile trade-off for the substantial improvement in read latency and write velocity, aligning perfectly with your requirement for repeated decompression on a single thread.<|im_end|>
